_note: Williams at the São Paulo Grand Prix 2024 (meeting 1249): what the respond stage (race/logistics.py) assumes about spares, chassis, hours, freight and allocations. Every number carries its basis: press (a published figure, with its source) or assumption (ours, with the reasoning). Williams does not publish its spares count; the press anchors are Vowles' own words.

vowles_spares.note: James Vowles, FIA Qatar 2024 Friday press conference: a team typically holds four or five of each component, and is in trouble after five or six crashes.

chassis_count.note: Williams had no spare chassis in Australia 2024; three chassis were built for 2024, the third arriving by Miami.

damage_tally.note: Vowles after Brazil: the recent crashes cost more than $3m and destroyed five front wings, five floors, five rear wings, three gearboxes, two engines and two chassis.

brazil_cost.note: Auto Motor und Sport, as reported by RacingNews365: the Brazil weekend's crashes cost Williams about $4m. race/prices.py is calibrated to land near it.

spares._why: Vowles' four or five of each component, less what Mexico (Albon's lap-1 retirement) and the season had already used: the truck arrived in São Paulo short. at_track travels with the team to Las Vegas; factory is finished stock at Grove.

power_unit._why: power unit elements come from the supplier's pool against the driver's allocation, not from Williams stock

chassis._why: three chassis built (press): two race cars and one bare spare tub that travels with the team

spare_tub_build_hours.why: a bare tub has to take the power unit, gearbox, suspension, loom, cooling and bodywork, then fire up and pass the checks: an overnight job for both crews

repair.why: hours to change one damaged part like for like in the garage; two crews work the front and the rear of the car at once, then the car fires up and is checked
repair.tub_at_track: a damaged monocoque is not repaired at the track: it goes back to Grove

decision.why: the team principal decides an hour before the start so the stewards and the Technical Delegate can be told before the pit exit opens
decision.points_why: expected points from a grid slot: the mean points of finishing within five places of it, times the chance of finishing (0.75, a wet Interlagos), and never less than a pit-lane start; a pit-lane start in a 20-car field rarely scores

freight.why: a flyaway after a flyaway: the race kit goes straight from São Paulo; parts made at Grove join the factory's last air consolidation, and anything later travels as hand carry with a person on a passenger flight

allocation.why: the power unit limits (ICE, TC, MGU-H, MGU-K 4; ES, CE 2 per driver) are the 2024 Sporting Regulations'; the gearbox limit of 4 and every count used by round 21 are ours: both cars at their limits on most elements, as most of the field was by Brazil. Colapinto inherited Sargeant's usage.
